verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Seobility, crawl an owned site, track selected keywords, and organize remediation tasks. The hard boundary is hosted crawling, keyword data, backlink monitoring, reports, and support, plus crawl scale, rule depth, and operational polish.
coreLoopDIY: Crawl a user-owned site, track selected keywords, inspect HTML and rendered pages, explain prioritized issues, organize remediation tasks, and export a reproducible audit.
requirements: permission to crawl the target site
whatYouLose: hosted crawling, keyword data, backlink monitoring, reports, and support
moatNotes: crawl scale, rule depth, and operational polish
ongoingBurden: robots handling, rendering, canonicalization, deduplication, crawl traps, rule maintenance, scheduling, storage, and false positives
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Seobility because a crawler is buildable; professionals pay for years of edge-case handling and reports they can trust with clients. The recurring cost buys robots handling, rendering, canonicalization, deduplication, crawl traps, rule maintenance, scheduling, storage, and false positives, not just the visible interface.

alternatives.name: CrawlSEO
alternatives.desc: Crawls, rank snapshots, alerts and issue history; replacing the subscription means adopting Postgres and Google OAuth.

facts.install: Clone the repository, configure environment variables, and start its Docker/PostgreSQL stack
facts.dataFormat: Sites, crawl snapshots, issues, keyword/rank observations, alerts, task history, users, and OAuth tokens live in the self-hosted PostgreSQL database; crawled page content and reports are retained by that deployment rather than a vendor cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: CrawlSEO combines crawling and rank history, but setup requires PostgreSQL and Google OAuth and its audit rules, reporting, collaboration, and remediation workflow are less mature than Seobility's.
facts.setupBlocker: The first real obstacle is infrastructure plus identity: Docker and PostgreSQL, a public callback URL, and a Google Cloud OAuth application before Search Console-backed ranking and alerts work.

alternatives.name: OpenSEO
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted audit and rank dashboard; remediation is a list rather than a workflow, and DataForSEO keeps the meter running.

facts.install: Clone the repository, supply environment variables, and run the documented Docker-based web/database deployment
facts.dataFormat: Projects, audits, issue results, tracked keywords, and historical observations live in the operator-controlled application database; keyword and SERP requests sent through DataForSEO leave the server and are retained/billed under that provider's account terms.
facts.gapVsPaid: OpenSEO can audit and track ranks, but DataForSEO remains metered and its issue list, reporting, collaboration, and guided remediation are much thinner than Seobility's.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert needs Docker, a database, authentication and email configuration, plus a funded DataForSEO account and API credentials, the rank tracker is not actually zero-cost to operate.

alternatives.name: SEO Panel
alternatives.desc: Site audits, keyword positions and reports in a maintained interface that still remembers Internet Explorer.

facts.install: Upload the PHP application to a web server, create a MySQL database, and complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Sites, users, keyword positions, audit results, reports, logs, and plugin configuration live in the configured MySQL/MariaDB database; application code, cached files, exports, and configuration remain on the PHP host.
facts.gapVsPaid: SEO Panel is genuinely self-hosted, but its dated interface, manual cron and plugin upkeep, crawler depth, reporting, and search-engine resilience lag far behind Seobility.
facts.setupBlocker: The first hurdle is a traditional PHP/MySQL deployment with writable directories and cron jobs; after that, search-engine changes and third-party plugins make maintenance much more manual than Seobility.

alternatives.name: Seobility Basic
alternatives.desc: The vendor's own permanent free tier covers one 1,000-page site and ten weekly-tracked keywords; small really does mean small.

facts.install: Hosted signup, add one website, and optionally verify ownership/connect Search Console
facts.dataFormat: Crawl snapshots, issue lists, task state, keyword positions, project settings, and connected-account metadata live in Seobility's cloud; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: The vendor's free tier is effortless but capped at one 1,000-page project and ten weekly tracked keywords, so it stops being a replacement as soon as the site or keyword set grows.

rejectedAlternatives.name: SEO PowerSuite Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Good one-off audits, no free project saving; remediation history vanishes with the window.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a single-site audit tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Seobility in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, Playwright, and an HTMX interface; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: crawl a user-owned site, track selected keywords, inspect HTML and rendered pages, explain prioritized issues, organize remediation tasks, and export a reproducible audit.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Require an explicit ownership or permission acknowledgement before a crawl starts.
Respect robots.txt, rate limits, canonical URLs, nofollow, redirects, and a configurable URL cap.
Collect status, title, description, headings, canonical, robots, links, images, structured data, and rendered text.
Detect duplicates, orphan candidates, broken links, redirect chains, missing metadata, and indexability conflicts.
Show every issue with affected URLs, evidence, severity, and a concrete remediation note.
Export crawl data and issues to CSV plus a self-contained HTML report.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out crawling sites without permission.
Deliberately leave out web-scale backlink or keyword datasets.
Deliberately leave out automated changes to production websites.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
